name: OpenRouter hosted API router
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, representative model meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct ROUTED TO GROQ, re-verified 2026-10-16. OpenRouter is a router, not a hoster: the same model id fans out to DeepInfra, Novita, AkashML, Parasail, Cloudflare, SambaNova, Groq, CoreWeave, Google Vertex and Together, each with its own upstream price that OpenRouter passes through with a markup baked into the listed rate. The 2026-10-16 provider table still spans $0.10/$0.32 (DeepInfra Turbo) to $1.04/$1.04 (Together); every list price is unchanged from the 2026-10-14 snapshot. price_input/price_output here stay the GROQ row ($0.59/$0.79) — the highest-throughput backend — not the floor. The page headline now prints the floor route ($0.10/$0.32) as 'the' price; that is a different claim and is named here rather than written into the scalar fields. Cache-read on Groq is still $0.295. No single 'OpenRouter price' exists for a model; quote provider+model or nothing.
notes: OpenRouter's own routing telemetry is the measurement: its model pages publish per-provider P50 latency, throughput and uptime measured over real routed traffic. Re-read 2026-10-16, Groq row on llama-3.3-70b-instruct: 0.52s P50 latency, 193 tok/s, 100.00% uptime. That replaces the 2026-10-14 Groq row (0.40s, 233 tok/s, 100% uptime) — same source, same model, two days later, ~17% slower. The old pair is kept here so the drift is visible rather than overwritten. measurement_source 'self' means measured-by-the-service-itself over production traffic, a different claim from both a vendor marketing number and the Artificial Analysis medians stored on the individual provider records (Groq's own record carries the AA figure, not this one). context_window is per-model-per-provider; 131072 is the llama-3.3-70b figure. Balanced/Nitro/Floor/Exacto routing modes pick different providers for the same request, so 'where does it run' is a routing decision, not a property of the endpoint. Other rows that moved on the same page, not promoted into the scalar fields: DeepInfra Turbo 0.48s / 16 tps (was 0.51s / 14), Novita 1.05s / 44 tps (was 0.58s / 41), SambaNova Turbo 0.81s / 104 tps (was 0.77s / 98). CoreWeave is the latency floor at 0.12s / 85 tps and $0.71/$0.71. Vertex and Together published no latency cell on this read. Billing goes through OpenRouter regardless of which upstream serves the request.
